target: Five deployment batches must each pass stage 1 and then stage 2, with both stages processing at most one batch at a time. Every batch must use the same order at both stages; waiting between stages is allowed. Processing times (stage1,stage2) are A=(3,8), B=(12,4), C=(6,7), D=(2,9), E=(10,3). The team must choose an order minimizing the time when all batches finish and compute that makespan.
surface: A previous deployment plan sorted batches by total processing time, shortest first, and did not distinguish whether a short operation occurred on stage 1 or stage 2.
structural: A two-machine flow shop minimized makespan with Johnson's rule. Repeatedly find the smallest unscheduled processing time across both machines: if it is on machine 1 place that job at the earliest open position; if on machine 2 place it at the latest open position. Then simulate machine 2 starts as max(its availability, that job's machine-1 completion).
rubric: Explicitly selects Johnson's two-machine flow-shop rule.
Builds a valid Johnson order D,A,C,B,E (tie-equivalent valid optimum accepted).
Simulates stage-1 completions 2,5,11,23,33 and stage-2 completions 11,19,26,30,36 for that order.
Reports a makespan of 36 and recommends the optimal order.
States the two-machine same-order/no-preemption assumptions or notes ties may allow another optimal sequence.
